summary: This study describes the molecular layer deposition (MLD) of a highly stable silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) thin film using bis(trichlorosilyl)methane and water as precursors at room temperature. The process avoids plasma, high temperatures, or highly oxidizing precursors by utilizing a nonoxidizing co-reactant. The resulting SiOC films exhibit exceptional thermal and chemical stability, with a cross-linked network structure, and are suitable for applications requiring low-k dielectric properties.
evidence: In this study, molecular layer deposition (MLD) was used to deposit ultrathin films of methylene-bridged silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) using bis(trichlorosilyl)-methane and water as precursors at room temperature. By utilizing bifunctional trichlorosilane precursors, films of SiOC can be deposited in a layer-by-layer manner, wherein a water co-reactant circumvents the need for plasma, high temperatures, or highly oxidizing precursors.
